0.long_answer: Lhermitte-Duclos disease, also known as dysplastic gangliocytoma of the cerebellum, is a rare and slow-growing tumor of the cerebellum. It is characterized by the presence of hypertrophic ganglion cells within the cerebellar cortex and is sometimes regarded as a hamartoma due to its benign nature and developmental origin. This tumor is notably associated with Cowden syndrome, a genetic disorder marked by multiple hamartomas and an increased risk of certain cancers.
